mechanism_narrative: A sustained high federal funds rate (above 5.0%) compresses equity valuations through elevated discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0%, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases across all historical periods.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate above 4.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that trigger equity sell-offs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE exceeds 4.0%, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous expansion in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 3-month moving averages signals robust economic momentum, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS and HOUST both exceed their 3-month moving averages, the 20-day forward returns are positive in less than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A supply expansion regime (INDPRO > 100) indicates improving manufacturing capacity, reducing inflationary pressures and supporting positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: In periods when INDPRO exceeds 100, the 60-day forward returns are positive in less than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1 > 2.0% annualized) reflects sustained economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 60 days through improved corporate earnings outlook.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 exceeds 2.0% annualized, the 60-day forward returns are positive in less than 40% of historical periods.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated year-over-year CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.5%) triggers central bank hawkishness and equity risk aversion, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.5%, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A tight labor market (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and UNRATE < 3.8%) accelerates wage growth and corporate profit margins, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5% and UNRATE falls below 3.8%, the 5-day forward returns are positive in less than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Housing market recovery (HOUST > 1300 thousand units) signals strengthening consumer confidence and spending, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: When HOUST exceeds 1300 thousand units, the 20-day forward returns are positive in less than 40% of instances.
